source.title: Two-Phase Dynamics of Interactions Explains the Starting Point of a DNN Learning Over-Fitted Features
source.authors: Jun-Peng Zhang; Qing Li; Liang Lin; Quan-Shi Zhang

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the paper and appendices; no apparent truncation or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: Measures how interaction complexity and its generalization power change during training, and reports alignment with the train–test loss gap using a different measure from the mapped versions.
record.gate_note: Results bear on V7's measured-property relationship: interaction order tracks generalization power, and the dynamics of interaction orders align temporally with the training–testing loss gap. The paper does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with norm- or margin-based measures. It also does not test the mapped architecture, optimizer, batch-size, explicit-regularization, or model-width comparisons, nor memorization of random labels.
record.test_reason: The study measures interaction order, training–test interaction similarity, and their training dynamics. These do not test V7's magnitude-aware weight sharpness or any other specified version. Its label-noise experiment measures interaction complexity, without reporting random-label fitting or held-out accuracy required by V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors report two-phase interaction dynamics across the tested networks, weaker training–test similarity for higher-order interactions, and temporal alignment with loss-gap growth. They interpret the second phase as the beginning of learning overfitted features, while noting that generalizable features and improving test accuracy can coexist with this process.
record.recipe_differences: Measures interaction strength by order and training–testing Jaccard similarity, rather than perturbation-based magnitude-aware sharpness. Reports temporal alignment with loss gaps rather than ranking sharpness measures.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported pattern spans model architectures and datasets; interaction measurement uses sampled middle-feature patches, tokens, or point clusters depending on modality.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 3 reports decreasing training–test interaction-distribution Jaccard similarity with increasing interaction order, averaged over the first 10 categories.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Higher-order interactions transfer less consistently between training and test samples than lower-order interactions.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 2 reports initial suppression of medium- and high-order interactions followed by learning interactions of increasing order, temporally aligned with widening training–test loss gaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Interaction complexity follows two training phases associated with changes in the training–test loss gap.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 4 reports higher-order interactions for incorrectly labeled examples than for original examples. Appendix C selects low-confidence examples and assigns their second-best category.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Classifying deliberately mislabeled, selected examples involves more complex interactions than classifying original examples.

record.problems: Key results are shown in figures without numeric values in the supplied text. The interaction generalization comparison averages over only the first 10 categories. The authors describe temporal alignment but provide no uncertainty estimates in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible result rows for the mapped versions: the study does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or the listed architecture, optimization, batch-size, regularization, width, or memorized-example interventions. Its interaction-order and Jaccard findings are not the measures named by V7, so they are recorded under fits_no_version rather than as V7 rows.

untested.parts: Natural-label versus fixed-random-label training fit and held-out accuracy. Selected low-confidence examples receive second-best labels; their interaction complexity does not establish V1.
Test error as width increases beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected test performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning or recovery recipes.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out error across training-set sizes and regularization settings.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation tolerance, its correlation with generalization gaps among comparably fitted networks, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized training examples versus random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's V7 tested status to not tested. Interaction complexity is a different construct from magnitude-aware sharpness. Section 3.4 uses the onset of loss-gap growth to annotate the phase boundary, so the reported alignment is not an independently estimated prediction of that boundary. No eligible version results require additional rows.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train on fixed random labels or compare natural-label and random-label test accuracy.
No width sweep or comparison around the zero-training-error threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison.
Tests whether interaction order and interaction generalization power relate to the train–test loss gap, but does not test magnitude-aware sharpness or rank it against norm- and margin-based measures.
Does not remove memorized examples and retrain.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
